cases.sentence: Стояли в ней: большой письменный ___ перед диваном, обитым клеенкой, бюро, шкаф в углу и несколько стульев.
cases.translation: In it stood: a large writing desk in front of a couch upholstered in oilcloth, a bureau, a cupboard in the corner, and several chairs.
cases.explain: "Стол" is part of the list of subjects of "стояли" (stood), so it is in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Он вдруг ощутил, что мнительность его, от одного ___ с Порфирием, уже разрослась в одно мгновение в чудовищные размеры…
cases.translation: He suddenly felt that his suspicion, from just one contact with Porfiry, had in an instant grown to monstrous proportions…
cases.explain: The preposition "от" (from) governs the genitive case, giving "соприкосновения."

cases.sentence: Как бы кидаясь то к окну, то к бюро, то опять к ___, то избегая подозрительного взгляда Раскольникова.
cases.translation: As if darting now to the window, now to the bureau, now again to the table, now avoiding Raskolnikov's suspicious gaze.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (toward) always governs the dative case, giving "столу."

cases.sentence: Он тотчас же пошел прямо к делу, встал с места и взял ___.
cases.translation: He went straight to the point at once, rose from his seat, and took his cap.
cases.explain: "Фуражку" is the direct object of the transitive verb "взял" (took), so it stands in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Он приготовился войти с холодным и дерзким ___ и дал себе слово как можно больше молчать.
cases.translation: He prepared to go in with a cold and insolent look and vowed to himself to keep silent as much as possible.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) describing manner governs the instrumental case, giving "видом."

cases.sentence: Оказалось, что в эту минуту Порфирий Петрович был у себя в ___ один.
cases.translation: It turned out that at that moment Porfiry Petrovich was alone in his office.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" marking location governs the prepositional case, giving "кабинете."

reading.ru: Когда на другое утро, ровно в одиннадцать часов, Раскольников вошел в дом —й части, в отделение пристава следственных дел, и попросил доложить о себе Порфирию Петровичу, то он даже удивился тому, как долго не принимали его: прошло, по крайней мере, десять минут, пока его позвали.
reading.question: How long did Raskolnikov wait before being received by Porfiry?
reading.correct: About ten minutes
reading.explain: The text says at least ten minutes passed before he was called in, which surprised him.

reading.ru: Беспокойным и подозрительным взглядом следил он кругом себя, высматривая: нет ли около него хоть какого-нибудь конвойного, какого-нибудь таинственного взгляда, назначенного его стеречь, чтоб он куда не ушел?
reading.question: What was Raskolnikov anxiously looking for while he waited?
options: A guard or watcher assigned to prevent him from leaving
reading.correct: A guard or watcher assigned to prevent him from leaving
reading.explain: He scanned the room with a restless, suspicious look for any guard or mysterious watcher set to keep him from escaping.

reading.ru: Оказалось, что в эту минуту Порфирий Петрович был у себя в кабинете один.
reading.question: In what state did Raskolnikov find Porfiry when finally admitted?
reading.correct: Alone in his office
reading.explain: It turned out that Porfiry Petrovich was alone in his office at that moment.

reading.ru: — А, почтеннейший! Вот и вы… в наших краях… — начал Порфирий, протянув ему обе руки.
reading.question: How does Porfiry greet Raskolnikov?
options: Warmly, extending both hands and calling him "most esteemed"
Coldly, refusing to look at him
reading.correct: Warmly, extending both hands and calling him "most esteemed"
reading.explain: Porfiry greets him cheerfully, calling him "most esteemed" and stretching out both hands.

reading.ru: «Он, однако ж, мне обе руки-то протянул, а ни одной ведь не дал, отнял вовремя», — мелькнуло в нем подозрительно.
reading.question: What suspicious detail does Raskolnikov notice about Porfiry's handshake gesture?
options: Porfiry extended both hands but gave neither, withdrawing them in time
Porfiry refused to shake hands at all
Porfiry wore gloves the whole time
reading.correct: Porfiry extended both hands but gave neither, withdrawing them in time
reading.explain: Raskolnikov suspiciously notices that Porfiry stretched out both hands yet never actually gave him one, pulling back in time.

reading.ru: — Я вам принес эту бумажку… об часах-то… вот-с.
reading.question: What object does Raskolnikov say he has brought to Porfiry?
reading.correct: A paper about the watch
reading.explain: Raskolnikov says he has brought the paper concerning the watch (the pawned item).

reading.ru: И он вдруг ощутил, что мнительность его, от одного соприкосновения с Порфирием, от двух только слов, от двух только взглядов, уже разрослась в одно мгновение в чудовищные размеры…
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov's suspicion change after just a few words and glances from Porfiry?
options: It grows instantly to monstrous proportions
reading.correct: It grows instantly to monstrous proportions
reading.explain: The text says his suspiciousness, from just a couple of words and glances, instantly swelled to monstrous proportions.

reading.ru: Чрезвычайно странною казалась при этом его маленькая, толстенькая и круглая фигурка, как будто мячик, катавшийся в разные стороны и тотчас отскакивавший от всех стен и углов.
reading.question: What image does the narrator use to describe Porfiry's figure as he paces?
options: A little ball bouncing off the walls and corners
A tall thin shadow gliding by
reading.correct: A little ball bouncing off the walls and corners
reading.explain: The narrator compares Porfiry's small, plump, round figure to a ball rolling about and bouncing off every wall and corner.

reading.ru: Успеем-с, успеем-с!.. А вы курите? Есть у вас? Вот-с, папиросочка-с…
reading.question: What does Porfiry offer Raskolnikov during their conversation?
reading.correct: A cigarette
reading.explain: Porfiry offers Raskolnikov a little cigarette while chatting.

reading.ru: — Да, славная вещь, — ответил Раскольников, почти с насмешкой смотря на него.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov respond when Porfiry praises the government apartment?
options: He agrees mockingly, "Yes, a fine thing"
He storms out of the room
reading.correct: He agrees mockingly, "Yes, a fine thing"
reading.explain: Raskolnikov answers, "Yes, a fine thing," while looking at Porfiry almost mockingly.

reading.ru: такой прием юридический — для всех возможных следователей — сперва начать издалека, с пустячков, или даже с серьезного, но только совсем постороннего, чтобы, так сказать, ободрить или, лучше сказать, развлечь допрашиваемого, усыпить его осторожность и потом вдруг, неожиданнейшим образом огорошить его в самое темя каким-нибудь самым роковым и опасным вопросом
reading.question: What legal interrogation tactic does Raskolnikov accuse Porfiry of using?
options: Starting from afar with trivial matters before suddenly striking with the most dangerous question
Bringing in false witnesses right away
reading.correct: Starting from afar with trivial matters before suddenly striking with the most dangerous question
reading.explain: Raskolnikov describes the classic tactic of starting with trifles to lull the suspect before suddenly hitting him with the most fatal question.

reading.ru: он вдруг залился нервным, продолжительным смехом, волнуясь и колыхаясь всем телом и прямо смотря в глаза Раскольникову.
reading.question: How does Porfiry react after Raskolnikov's remark about interrogation tactics?
options: He bursts into prolonged nervous laughter while staring at Raskolnikov
reading.correct: He bursts into prolonged nervous laughter while staring at Raskolnikov
reading.explain: Porfiry breaks into a long, nervous fit of laughter, his whole body shaking, while staring straight into Raskolnikov's eyes.

reading.ru: Он тотчас же пошел прямо к делу, встал с места и взял фуражку.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do after growing irritated with Porfiry's rambling?
options: He stands up and takes his cap, ready to leave
He falls asleep in his chair
reading.correct: He stands up and takes his cap, ready to leave
reading.explain: Raskolnikov gets straight to the point, rising from his seat and taking his cap as if to go.

reading.ru: Мне надо быть на похоронах того самого раздавленного лошадьми чиновника, про которого вы… тоже знаете…
reading.question: What event does Raskolnikov say he needs to attend?
options: The funeral of the official who was run over by horses
reading.correct: The funeral of the official who was run over by horses
reading.explain: Raskolnikov says he must attend the funeral of the official who was trampled by horses, referring to Marmeladov.

reading.ru: Я, знаете, человек холостой, этак несветский и неизвестный, и к тому же законченный человек, закоченелый человек-с
reading.question: How does Porfiry describe himself to Raskolnikov?
options: An unmarried, unsociable and obscure man
A married man with many children
reading.correct: An unmarried, unsociable and obscure man
reading.explain: Porfiry describes himself as a bachelor, unsocial and unknown, and a stiff, finished sort of man.

reading.ru: Кофеем вас не прошу-с, не место; но минуток пять времени почему не посидеть с приятелем, для развлечения
reading.question: What does Porfiry say he won't offer Raskolnikov, given it's not the place for it?
reading.correct: Coffee
reading.explain: Porfiry says he won't offer coffee since it isn't the place for it, but suggests sitting a few minutes as friends.

reading.ru: Дело следователя ведь это, так сказать, свободное художество, в своем роде-с или вроде того… хе-хе-хе!..
reading.question: How does Porfiry characterize the work of an investigator?
reading.correct: As a kind of "free art"
reading.explain: Porfiry calls the investigator's work a sort of free art, or something like that.

reading.ru: Раскольников вдруг заметил, что, бегая по комнате, он раза два точно как будто останавливался подле дверей, на одно мгновение, и как будто прислушивался…
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov notice about Porfiry's behavior near the door while pacing?
options: Porfiry seemed to pause and listen by the door
reading.correct: Porfiry seemed to pause and listen by the door
reading.explain: Raskolnikov notices that Porfiry, while running about the room, twice paused by the door for a moment as if listening.

reading.ru: Видали бабочку перед свечкой?
reading.question: What image does Porfiry use to describe how the psychologically cornered suspect will behave?
reading.correct: A moth circling a candle
reading.explain: Porfiry compares the suspect's behavior to a moth circling endlessly around a candle.

reading.ru: Порфирий Петрович! — проговорил он громко и отчетливо, хотя едва стоял на дрожавших ногах, — я, наконец, вижу ясно, что вы положительно подозреваете меня в убийстве этой старухи и ее сестры Лизаветы.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov finally declare to Porfiry directly?
options: That Porfiry clearly suspects him of murdering the old woman and her sister Lizaveta
That he is leaving Petersburg for good
That he wants to confess immediately
That he wants to hire a lawyer
reading.correct: That Porfiry clearly suspects him of murdering the old woman and her sister Lizaveta
reading.explain: Raskolnikov states loudly that he now clearly sees Porfiry positively suspects him of murdering the old woman and her sister Lizaveta.

reading.ru: Порфирий быстро отвернулся и побежал отворить окно.
reading.question: What does Porfiry do when Raskolnikov appears to have a fit?
options: He rushes to open the window for air
reading.correct: He rushes to open the window for air
reading.explain: Porfiry quickly turns and runs to open the window, seemingly worried about Raskolnikov's condition.

reading.ru: Вот и Дмитрий Прокофьич ко мне вчера приходил
reading.question: Who does Porfiry mention visited him the day before?
reading.correct: Dmitri Prokofyich (Razumikhin)
reading.explain: Porfiry mentions that Dmitri Prokofyich, that is Razumikhin, came to see him the day before.

reading.ru: одним словом, я хочу знать: признаете ли вы меня окончательно свободным от подозрений или нет?
reading.question: What direct demand does Raskolnikov make of Porfiry?
options: Whether Porfiry considers him finally free of suspicion or not
Whether Porfiry will marry his sister
Whether Porfiry will lend him money
Whether Porfiry knows where Sonya lives
reading.correct: Whether Porfiry considers him finally free of suspicion or not
reading.explain: Raskolnikov insists he wants to know, once and for all, whether Porfiry considers him free from suspicion.

reading.ru: Сюрпризик-с, вот тут, за дверью у меня сидит, хе-хе-хе!
reading.question: Where does Porfiry say the "surprise" is located?
reading.correct: Sitting behind a locked door
reading.explain: Porfiry says the little surprise is sitting right there, behind the door.

reading.ru: Но тут случилось странное происшествие, нечто до того неожиданное, при обыкновенном ходе вещей, что уже, конечно, ни Раскольников, ни Порфирий Петрович на такую развязку и не могли рассчитывать.
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: With a strange, unexpected event that neither man could have foreseen
reading.correct: With a strange, unexpected event that neither man could have foreseen
reading.explain: The chapter ends by noting that a strange, wholly unexpected event occurred that neither man could have anticipated.
